Er wird über die Header-Datei <code>Rte_EcuM_Type.h</code> bereitgestellt <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_91004" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_91004">[SWS_EcuM_91004]</a>.</p> <h4>Verwendung und Schnittstellen</h4> <p>In AUTOSAR-Port-Schnittstellen fungiert <code>EcuM_UserType</code> primär als Port-Defined Argument Value (PDA), über den die Identität des anfragenden Nutzers konfigurationsbasiert am Port festgelegt wird:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Zustandsanforderungen:</strong> An Ports vom Typ <code>StateRequest_{UserName}</code> (Interface <code>EcuM_StateRequest</code>) zur Steuerung von Betriebszuständen <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04135" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04135">[SWS_EcuM_04135]</a>. Die Benutzer-ID wird bei den synchronen Diensten <code>EcuM_RequestRUN</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04124" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04124">[SWS_EcuM_04124]</a>, <code>EcuM_ReleaseRUN</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04127" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04127">[SWS_EcuM_04127]</a> sowie <code>EcuM_RequestPOST_RUN</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04128" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04128">[SWS_EcuM_04128]</a> und <code>EcuM_ReleasePOST_RUN</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04129" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04129">[SWS_EcuM_04129]</a> ausgewertet. Zudem autorisiert <code>EcuM_UserType</code> den Aufruf von <code>EcuM_GoDownHaltPoll</code> für das Einleiten von Schlafmodi oder Abschaltvorgängen <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_91002" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_91002">[SWS_EcuM_91002]</a>.</li> <li><strong>Weckalarm-Verwaltung:</strong> An Ports vom Typ <code>AlarmClock_{UserName}</code> (Interface <code>EcuM_AlarmClock</code>) <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_03017" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_03017">[SWS_EcuM_03017]</a>. Hierbei identifiziert der Typ den Besitzer von Weckzeiten bei Aufrufen von <code>EcuM_SetRelWakeupAlarm</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04054" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04054">[SWS_EcuM_04054]</a>, <code>EcuM_SetAbsWakeupAlarm</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04057" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04057">[SWS_EcuM_04057]</a>, <code>EcuM_AbortWakeupAlarm</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04061" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04061">[SWS_EcuM_04061]</a> und <code>EcuM_SetClock</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04064" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04064">[SWS_EcuM_04064]</a>.</li> </ul> <h4>Nebenläufigkeit und Einschränkungen</h4> <p>Die zugehörigen C-APIs sind durchgängig als synchron und reentrant definiert <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04054" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04054">[SWS_EcuM_04054]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04124" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04124">[SWS_EcuM_04124]</a>. Aufrufer müssen beachten, dass Anforderungen nur von Benutzern akzeptiert werden, die dem State Manager zur Konfigurationszeit bekannt gemacht wurden <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04124" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04124">[SWS_EcuM_04124]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_91002" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_91002">[SWS_EcuM_91002]</a>. Da Alarme nutzergebunden verwaltet werden, quittiert beispielsweise <code>EcuM_AbortWakeupAlarm</code> den Abbruch mit <code>ECUM_E_NOT_ACTIVE</code>, falls für die angegebene Benutzer-ID kein aktiver Alarm existiert <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04061" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04061">[SWS_EcuM_04061]</a>.</p> <p class="ai-note">Dieser Nutzungshinweis wurde automatisiert auf Basis der Spezifikation von AUTOSAR Classic R20-11 erstellt.</p> </div>

# Richtlinien für KI-generierte Erklärungen

Diese Datei wird von den Prompt-Rezepten (`_src/tools/prompt_recipes.py`)
wörtlich in jeden Prompt eingebettet. Jede Änderung ändert daher alle
Prompt-Hashes; bestehende KI-Texte gelten dann als veraltet und werden neu
erzeugt. Herkunft und Ablage der Ausgaben regelt `_src/lib_ai_store.py`.

## Sprache

- Kanonische Sprache ist Deutsch. Die Übersetzung ist ein nachgelagerter Schritt
  und nie Teil der Generierung.
- API-Bezeichner, Typnamen, Enum-Werte, Code und Kennungen wie `[SWS_…]` bleiben
  unverändert.

## Struktur

- Jedes Fragment ist genau ein `<div class="ai …">` (Varianten: `ai usage` für
  Verwendungshinweise an einem Spezifikationselement, `ai module-guide` für
  Modul-Leitfäden) und endet mit genau einem `<p class="ai-note">` (KI-Hinweis).
- Erlaubte Elemente im Fragment: `div`, `p`, `h4`, `ul`, `ol`, `li`, `code`,
  `strong`, `em`, `a`, `span`, `table`, `thead`, `tbody`, `tr`, `th`, `td`.
  Keine Skripte, keine Stile, keine Bilder, kein `<svg>` (Diagramme siehe unten).
- Alle Tags korrekt geschlossen und verschachtelt.

## Belegpflicht

- Jede fachliche Aussage ist zu belegen. Belege stammen ausschließlich aus dem
  Payload des Prompts; nichts darf aus anderem Wissen als Beleg ausgegeben werden.
- Verweis auf ein Spezifikationselement oder Requirement (nur IDs, die im
  Payload vorkommen):
  `<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_…">[SWS_…]</a>` — ohne `href`; den
  Link setzt der Generator.
- Verweis auf eine Dokumentstelle (nur Dokument/Seite aus dem Payload):
  `<span class="docref" data-doc="<Dokument-ID>" data-page="<Seite>">Kurzname §x.y „Titel“</span>`.
- Niemals URLs ausgeben, insbesondere keine PDF-URLs.

## Annahmen (Wissenslücken)

- Wo die Quellen schweigen, sind höchstens 3 Annahmen je Text und 2 je
  Diagramm erlaubt.
- Jede Annahme ist im Text als Interpretation erkennbar („dürfte“, „vermutlich“,
  „Interpretation:“) und wird am Ende des Fragments in einem Kommentar
  `<!-- annahmen: 1) … – Begründung: … -->` aufgezählt.
- Reicht das Budget nicht, wird der Aspekt weggelassen — niemals unmarkiert
  spekulieren.

## Diagramme

Ein Diagramm nur, wenn es gegenüber dem Text Mehrwert bietet:

- Sequenzdiagramm: Abläufe ab 3 Schritten oder mit nicht offensichtlicher
  Reihenfolge/Asynchronität.
- Kontext-/Kollaborationsdiagramm: ab 3 beteiligten Komponenten.
- Zustandsdiagramm: Lebenszyklen und Zustandsmaschinen.
- Aktivitätsdiagramm: Entscheidungs- oder Verarbeitungsabläufe mit Verzweigung.
- Keine Trivialdiagramme (einzelne Aufrufe, Getter/Setter, Zweierbeziehungen).

Beschriftungen deutsch, Bezeichner unverändert. Jedes Diagramm steht im
Fragment als Platzhalter `<div class="diagram" id="diag-<kurzname>"></div>`,
direkt gefolgt von `<p class="diagram-note"><Diagrammart>: <Kernaussage>.
Quellen: <Belege></p>`. Die Diagrammquelle wird separat ausgegeben (Format
legt der Prompt fest).

A continuación se muestra la versión de referencia original.</div>
  <h4>Verwendung und Wertebereich</h4>
  <p>Der Typ <code>EcuM_StateType</code> ist von <code>uint8</code> abgeleitet und über die Header-Datei <code>EcuM.h</code> verfügbar <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_91005" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_91005">[SWS_EcuM_91005]</a>. Er bildet die Zustände des ECU State Managers ab, die vom EcuM-Modul vollständig definiert werden müssen <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02664" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02664">[SWS_EcuM_02664]</a>. Die Spezifikation definiert folgende Zustände und Masken <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_91005" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_91005">[SWS_EcuM_91005]</a>:</p>
  <ul>
    <li><code>ECUM_SUBSTATE_MASK</code> (0x0f)</li>
    <li><code>ECUM_STATE_STARTUP</code> (0x10)</li>
    <li><code>ECUM_STATE_RUN</code> (0x32)</li>
    <li><code>ECUM_STATE_POST_RUN</code> (0x33)</li>
    <li><code>ECUM_STATE_SHUTDOWN</code> (0x40)</li>
    <li><code>ECUM_STATE_SLEEP</code> (0x50)</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Zusammenspiel und Aufrufkontext</h4>
  <p><code>EcuM_StateType</code> dient als Datentyp für den Zustandsaustausch zwischen dem ECU State Manager (EcuM) und dem Basic Software Mode Manager (BswM):</p>
  <ul>
    <li><strong>Zustandswechsel durch BswM:</strong> Der BswM benachrichtigt den EcuM synchron und reentrant über einen Zustandswechsel mittels der Funktion <code>EcuM_SetState</code> (Service-ID <code>0x2b</code>), wobei der Zielzustand im Parameter <code>state</code> vom Typ <code>EcuM_StateType</code> übergeben wird <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04122" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04122">[SWS_EcuM_04122]</a>.</li>
    <li><strong>Statusrückmeldung an BswM:</strong> Der EcuM meldet dem BswM den aktuellen Zustand über die Schnittstelle <code>BswM_EcuM_CurrentState(EcuM_StateType State)</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04143" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04143">[SWS_EcuM_04143]</a>.</li>
  </ul>

  <h4>Reihenfolgebedingungen und Fehlerbehandlung</h4>
  <p>Ein neuer Zustand darf vom EcuM erst dann gesetzt werden, wenn das RTE seine Rückmeldung über den Bestätigungs-Port (acknowledgement port) bereitgestellt hat <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04143" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04143">[SWS_EcuM_04143]</a>.</p>
  <p>Als Typdefinition definiert <code>EcuM_StateType</code> keine eigenen Fehlercodes oder DET-/DEM-Meldungen <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_91005" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_91005">[SWS_EcuM_91005]</a>.</p>

  <p class="ai-note">Dieser Nutzungshinweis wurde automatisiert auf Basis der AUTOSAR-Spezifikation für R20-11 erstellt.</p>
</div>

=== SYSTEM PROMPT ===
Du bist der KI-Kurations-Assistent des Dokumentationssystems autodocs (AUTOSAR).
Verfasse den Modul-Leitfaden (<div class="ai module-guide">) für das classic-Modul 'ecum' im Release R20-11.

RICHTLINIEN (bindend):
# Richtlinien für KI-generierte Erklärungen

Diese Datei wird von den Prompt-Rezepten (`_src/tools/prompt_recipes.py`)
wörtlich in jeden Prompt eingebettet. Jede Änderung ändert daher alle
Prompt-Hashes; bestehende KI-Texte gelten dann als veraltet und werden neu
erzeugt. Herkunft und Ablage der Ausgaben regelt `_src/lib_ai_store.py`.

## Sprache

- Kanonische Sprache ist Deutsch. Die Übersetzung ist ein nachgelagerter Schritt
  und nie Teil der Generierung.
- API-Bezeichner, Typnamen, Enum-Werte, Code und Kennungen wie `[SWS_…]` bleiben
  unverändert.

## Struktur

- Jedes Fragment ist genau ein `<div class="ai …">` (Varianten: `ai usage` für
  Verwendungshinweise an einem Spezifikationselement, `ai module-guide` für
  Modul-Leitfäden) und endet mit genau einem `<p class="ai-note">` (KI-Hinweis).
- Erlaubte Elemente im Fragment: `div`, `p`, `h4`, `ul`, `ol`, `li`, `code`,
  `strong`, `em`, `a`, `span`, `table`, `thead`, `tbody`, `tr`, `th`, `td`.
  Keine Skripte, keine Stile, keine Bilder, kein `<svg>` (Diagramme siehe unten).
- Alle Tags korrekt geschlossen und verschachtelt.

## Belegpflicht

- Jede fachliche Aussage ist zu belegen. Belege stammen ausschließlich aus dem
  Payload des Prompts; nichts darf aus anderem Wissen als Beleg ausgegeben werden.
- Verweis auf ein Spezifikationselement oder Requirement (nur IDs, die im
  Payload vorkommen):
  `<a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_…">[SWS_…]</a>` — ohne `href`; den
  Link setzt der Generator.
- Verweis auf eine Dokumentstelle (nur Dokument/Seite aus dem Payload):
  `<span class="docref" data-doc="<Dokument-ID>" data-page="<Seite>">Kurzname §x.y „Titel“</span>`.
- Niemals URLs ausgeben, insbesondere keine PDF-URLs.

## Annahmen (Wissenslücken)

- Wo die Quellen schweigen, sind höchstens 3 Annahmen je Text und 2 je
  Diagramm erlaubt.
- Jede Annahme ist im Text als Interpretation erkennbar („dürfte“, „vermutlich“,
  „Interpretation:“) und wird am Ende des Fragments in einem Kommentar
  `<!-- annahmen: 1) … – Begründung: … -->` aufgezählt.
- Reicht das Budget nicht, wird der Aspekt weggelassen — niemals unmarkiert
  spekulieren.

## Diagramme

Ein Diagramm nur, wenn es gegenüber dem Text Mehrwert bietet:

- Sequenzdiagramm: Abläufe ab 3 Schritten oder mit nicht offensichtlicher
  Reihenfolge/Asynchronität.
- Kontext-/Kollaborationsdiagramm: ab 3 beteiligten Komponenten.
- Zustandsdiagramm: Lebenszyklen und Zustandsmaschinen.
- Aktivitätsdiagramm: Entscheidungs- oder Verarbeitungsabläufe mit Verzweigung.
- Keine Trivialdiagramme (einzelne Aufrufe, Getter/Setter, Zweierbeziehungen).

Beschriftungen deutsch, Bezeichner unverändert. Jedes Diagramm steht im
Fragment als Platzhalter `<div class="diagram" id="diag-<kurzname>"></div>`,
direkt gefolgt von `<p class="diagram-note"><Diagrammart>: <Kernaussage>.
Quellen: <Belege></p>`. Die Diagrammquelle wird separat ausgegeben (Format
legt der Prompt fest).

LEITBILD (Umfang und Aufbau orientieren sich an den bewährten Adaptive-Modulleitfäden):
- 900–1600 Wörter in 5–8 thematischen Abschnitten mit <h4>-Überschriften, die das
  Modul erschließen (z. B. Rolle und Systemgrenze, zentrale Abläufe vom Start bis zur
  Nutzung, Daten- und Interaktionsformen, Betriebsregeln und Randbedingungen,
  Konfiguration/Instanzbezug, Verhalten im Fehlerfall). Die Überschriften sind
  modulspezifisch zu formulieren, nicht generisch.
- Ein Abschnitt „Verhalten im Fehlerfall“ und am Ende ein Abschnitt
  „Weiterführende Detailbelege“ (die wichtigsten Requirements/Dokumentstellen kurz
  eingeordnet).
- Jeder Absatz enthält mindestens einen Beleg (Requirement-ID oder Dokumentstelle).
- 4–10 Diagramme, wo sie Mehrwert bieten: Sequenzdiagramme für zentrale Abläufe,
  Zustandsdiagramme für Lebenszyklen, Kontext-/Kollaborationsdiagramme für die
  Einbettung, Aktivitätsdiagramme für Entscheidungen. Die Schaubilder der Spezifikation
  (Payload-Einträge mit "figure": true) sind Ausgangspunkt: übernimm ihre Aussage,
  wo sie den Text stützen, und verbessere ihre Lesbarkeit.
- Das Fragment beginnt mit <div class="ai module-guide"> und endet mit
  <p class="ai-note">…</p></div>.

AUSGABEFORMAT (verbindlich, nichts außerhalb dieser Blöcke):
<<<FRAGMENT
<div class="…"> … </div>
FRAGMENT>>>
Danach je Diagramm-Platzhalter genau ein Block:
<<<DIAGRAM diag-<kurzname> seq
<JSON nach dem Sequenz-Schema>
DIAGRAM>>>
oder
<<<DIAGRAM diag-<kurzname> dot
<Graphviz-digraph ohne Stilattribute (Farben/Schriften setzt der Generator)>
DIAGRAM>>>

Sequenz-Schema (JSON):
{"titel": str, "teilnehmer": [{"name": str}], "schritte": [
  {"art": "nachricht", "von": <idx>, "nach": <idx>, "text": [str], "pfeil": "voll"|"offen", "gestrichelt": bool},
  {"art": "selbst", "teilnehmer": <idx>, "text": [str]},
  {"art": "notiz", "ueber": [<idx>, <idx>], "text": [str]},
  {"art": "abschnitt", "text": str},
  {"art": "rahmen", "typ": "alt"|"opt"|"loop", "guard": str}, {"art": "trenner", "guard": str}, {"art": "rahmen-ende"}
]}
Antworten/Rückgaben: "pfeil": "offen", "gestrichelt": true. Zustands-, Kontext- und Aktivitätsdiagramme als dot.

   "text": "The EcuM_SelectShutdownTarget function shall set the shut- down target to the value of the shutdownTarget parameter."

  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_01117",
   "text": "EcuM_SetWakeupEvent sets (OR-operation) all events passed as a bit set in the sources in parameter ( EcuM_WakeupSourceType bitmask) in the internal pending wakeup events variable."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_01156",
   "text": "EcuM_GetPendingWakeupEvents shall return wakeup events which have been set to pending but not yet validated as bits set in a EcuM_- WakeupSourceType bitmask."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02156",
   "text": "EcuM_GetLastShutdownTarget shall return the ECU state from which the last wakeup or power up occurred in the shutdownTarget parameter. EcuM_ GetLastShutdownTarget shall always return the same value until the next shutdown."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02157",
   "text": "EcuM_GetLastShutdownTarget may return a shutdown target in a STARTUP phase that set late in a previous SHUTDOWN phase. If so, implementation specific limitations shall be clearly documented."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02165",
   "text": "Additional wakeup sources (to the pre-defined sources) shall be assigned individually to bitfield positions 5 to 31 by configuration. The bit assignment shall be done by the configuration tool."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02166",
   "text": "The EcuMWakeupSourceId (see ECUC_EcuM_00151) field in the EcuMWakeupSource container shall define the position corresponding to that wakeup source in all instances the EcuM_WakeupSourceType bitfield."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02171",
   "text": "EcuM_SetWakeupEvent must be callable from interrupt con- text, from OS context and an OS-free context."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02172",
   "text": "EcuM_GetPendingWakeupEvents shall be callable from in- terrupt context, from OS context and an OS-free context."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02181",
   "text": "The ECU Manager module shall call EcuM_GetValidated- WakeupEvents with the configured default shutdown target ( EcuMDefaultShut- downTarget )."

  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02185",
   "text": "The parameter mode of the function EcuM_SelectShutdown Target shall be the identifier of a sleep or reset mode. The mode parameter shall only be used if the target parameter equals ECUM_SHUTDOWN_TARGET_SLEEP or ECUM_SHUTDOWN_TARGET_RESET. In all other cases, it shall be ignored. Only sleep or reset modes that are defined at configuration time and are stored in the Ecu MCommonConfiguration container (see ECUC_EcuM_00181) are allowed as parame- ters."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02188",
   "text": "No wakeup event shall be missed in the SLEEP phase. The Halt or Poll Sequences shall not be entered if a wakeup event has occurred in the Go Sleep sequence."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02247",
   "text": "The service EcuM_SelectBootTarget shall store the se- lected target in a way that is compatible with the boot loader."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02336",
   "text": "If the call of GetLastShutdownTarget() passes ECU_STATE_ SLEEP in the parameter shutdownTarget, in the parameter shutdownMode it returns which of the configured sleep modes was actually chosen. 112 of 210 Document ID 78: AUTOSAR_SWS_ECUStateManager Specification of ECU State Manager AUTOSAR CP R20-11 If the call of GetLastShutdownTarget() passes ECU_STATE_RESET in the parameter shutdownTarget, in the parameter sleepMode it returns which of the configured reset modes was actually chosen."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02337",
   "text": "If the pointer to the shutdownMode parameter is NULL, Ecu M_GetLastShutdownTarget shall simply ignore the shutdownMode parameter and re- turn the last shutdown target regardless of whether it was SLEEP or not. If Develop- ment Error Detection is activated, EcuM_GetShutdownTarget shall send the ECUM_ E_PARAM_POINTER development error to the DET module."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02345",
   "text": "EcuM_ValidateWakeupEvent shall be callable from interrupt context and task context."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02389",
   "text": "To set the wakeup sources up for the next sleep mode, the ECU Manager module shall execute the EcuM_EnableWakeupSources callout (see [SWS_EcuM_02546] ) for each wakeup source that is configured in EcuMWakeup- SourceMask for the target sleep mode."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02411",
   "text": "Table StartPreOS Sequence shows the activities in StartPre OS Sequence and the order in which they shall be executed in EcuM_Init (see [SWS_EcuM_02811] )."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02479",
   "text": "The ECU Manager module shall execute the Wakeup Valida- tion Protocol upon the EcuM_SetWakeupEvent (see [SWS_EcuM_02826] ) function call according to Interaction of Wakeup Sources and the ECU Manager later in this chapter."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02496",
   "text": "If the wakeup event is validated (either immediately or by the wakeup validation protocol), the ECU Manager module shall make the information that it is a source of the current ECU wakeup through the EcuM_GetValidatedWakeu- pEvents (see [SWS_EcuM_02830] ) function."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02532",
   "text": "EcuM_GetValidatedWakeupEvent shall be callable from in- terrupt context, from OS context and an OS-free context."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02533",
   "text": "EcuM_GetValidatedWakeupEvent shall return wakeup events which have been set to validated in the internal validated events variable as bits set in a EcuM_WakeupSourceType bitmask."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02539",
   "text": "If the ECU Manager module has a list of wakeup source can- didates when the WakeupRestart Sequence has finished, the ECU Manager module shall validate these wakeup source candidates in EcuM_MainFunction ."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02546",
   "text": "The ECU Manager module shall derive the wakeup sources to be enabled (and used as the wakeupSource parameter) from the EcuMWakeupSource (see ECUC_EcuM_00152) bitfield configured for the current sleep mode."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02559",
   "text": "The configuration of the ECU Manager module shall spec- ify the order of initialization calls inside init block 0 and init block 1. (see EcuM- DriverInitListZero and EcuMDriverInitListOne )."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02561",
   "text": "The ECU Manager module shall initialize the drivers in Ecu MDriverRestartList in the same order as in the combined list of init block 0 and init block 1."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02562",
   "text": "EcuMDriverRestartList may contain drivers that serve as wakeup sources. EcuM_AL_DriverRestart shall re-arm the trigger mechanism of these drivers' 'wakeup detected' callback."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02565",
   "text": "The ECU Manager module shall start a validation timeout for each pending wakeup event that should be validated. The timeout shall be event- specific (see EcuMValidationTimeout )."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02566",
   "text": "The ECU Manager module shall only invoke wakeup validation on those wakeup sources where it is required by configuration. If the validation protocol 60 of 210 Document ID 78: AUTOSAR_SWS_ECUStateManager Specification of ECU State Manager AUTOSAR CP R20-11 is not configured (see EcuMValidationTimeout ), then a call to EcuM_SetWakeu- pEvent shall also imply a call to EcuM_ValidateWakeupEvent ."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02572",
   "text": "The ECU Manager module shall detect wakeups that occurr prior to driver initialization, both from Halt/Poll or from OFF."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02585",
   "text": "EcuM_SelectShutdownTarget shall not initiate any setup activi- ties but only store the value for later use in the SHUTDOWN or SLEEP phase."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02589",
   "text": "EcuM_GetExpiredWakeupEvents shall be callable from in- terrupt context, from OS context and an OS-free context."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02601",
   "text": "If the EcuM cannot determine the reset reason returned by the Mcu driver, then the EcuM set a wakeup event for default wakeup source ECUM_ WKSOURCE_RESET instead."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02603",
   "text": "The StartPreOS Sequence shall initialize all basic software modules that are needed to start the OS."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02623",
   "text": "The ECU Manager module shall remember the wakeup source resulting from the reset reason translation (see table StartPreOS Sequence )."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02625",
   "text": "The ECU Manager module shall never invoke validation for the following wakeup sources: • ECUM_WKSOURCE_POWER • ECUM_WKSOURCE_RESET • ECUM_WKSOURCE_INTERNAL_RESET 63 of 210 Document ID 78: AUTOSAR_SWS_ECUStateManager Specification of ECU State Manager AUTOSAR CP R20-11 • ECUM_WKSOURCE_INTERNAL_WDG • ECUM_WKSOURCE_EXTERNAL_WDG."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02645",
   "text": "EcuM_ValidateWakeupEvent shall invoke ComM_EcuM_ WakeUpIndication for each wakeup event if the EcuMComMChannelRef parameter (see ECUC_EcuM_00101) in the EcuMWakeupSource configuration container for the corresponding wakeup source is configured."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02664",
   "text": "The ECU Manager module shall define all states as listed in the EcuM_StateType."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02683",
   "text": "EcuM_ClearWakeupEvent clears all pending events passed as a bit set in the sources in parameter (EcuM_WakeupSourceType bitmask) from the internal pending wakeup events variable, the internal validated events variable and the internal expired events variable."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02684",
   "text": "When activated through the EcuM_Init (see [SWS_EcuM_02811] ) function, the ECU Manager module shall perform the ac- tions in the StartPreOS Sequence (see table StartPreOS Sequence )."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02707",
   "text": "EcuM_SetWakeupEvent shall start the wakeup validation timeout timer according to Wakeup Validation Timeout ."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02709",
   "text": "The ECU Manager module shall start the wakeup validation timeout timer when EcuM_SetWakeupEvent (see [SWS_EcuM_02826] ) is called."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02710",
   "text": "EcuM_ValidateWakeupEvent shall stop the wakeup valida- tion timeout timer (see [SWS_EcuM_02829] )."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02712",
   "text": "If EcuM_SetWakeupEvent (see [SWS_EcuM_02826] ) is called subsequently for the same wakeup source, the ECU Manager module shall not restart the wakeup validation timeout."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02730",
   "text": "The ECU Manager module shall call each driver's init function with the parameters derived from the driver's EcuMModuleService configuration con- tainer."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02756",
   "text": "When a wakeup event occurs during the shutdown phase, the ECU Manager module shall complete the shutdown and restart immediately there- after."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02788",
   "text": "If the pointer to the shutdownMode parameter is NULL, EcuM_ GetShutdownTarget shall simply ignore the shutdownMode parameter. If Development Error Detection is activated, EcuM_GetShutdownTarget shall send the ECUM_E_ PARAM_POINTER development error to the DET module."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02790",
   "text": "EcuM_ValidateWakeupEvent shall return without effect for all sources except communication channels when called while the ECU Manager mod- ule is in the RUN state."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02791",
   "text": "EcuM_ValidateWakeupEvent shall have full effect in any ECU Phase for those sources that correspond to a communication channel (see [SWS_EcuM_02645])."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02794",
   "text": "The structure defined in the EcuM_ConfigType type shall con- tain an additional post-build configuration variant identifier (uint8/uint16/uint32 depend- ing on algorithm to compute the identifier)."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02795",
   "text": "The structure defined by the EcuM_ConfigType type shall con- tain an additional hash code that is tested against the configuration parameter EcuM- ConfigConsistencyHash for checking consistency of the configuration data."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02796",
   "text": "The ECU Manager module shall not only check the consistency of its own parameters but of all post-build configurable BSW modules before initializing the first BSW module."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02798",
   "text": "The ECU Manager module shall check in EcuM_Init (see [SWS_EcuM_02811] ) that the field in the structure is equal to the value of ECUM_ CONFIGCONSISTENCY_HASH ."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02799",
   "text": "The hash computation algorithm used to compute a hash value over all pre-compile and link-time configuration parameters of all BSW modules shall always produce the same hash value for the same set of configuration data regardless of the order of configuration parameters in the XML files."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02801",
   "text": "The structure defined by type EcuM_ConfigType shall hold the post-build configuration parameters for the ECU Manager module as well as pointers to all ConfigType structures of modules that are initialized by the ECU Manager module."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02806",
   "text": "Caveats of EcuM_StartupTwo: This function must be called from a task, which is started directly as a consequence of StartOS. I.e. either the EcuM_StartupTwo function must be called from an autostart task or the EcuM_Startup Two function must be called from a task, which is explicitly started."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02807",
   "text": "EcuM_ClearWakeupEvent shall be callable from interrupt con- text, from OS context and an OS-free context."
  },

  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02863",
   "text": "The ECU Manager module shall invoke the EcuM_Generat- eRamHash (see [SWS_EcuM_02919] ) callout before halting the microcontroller the 49 of 210 Document ID 78: AUTOSAR_SWS_ECUStateManager Specification of ECU State Manager AUTOSAR CP R20-11 EcuM_CheckRamHash (see [SWS_EcuM_02921] ) callout after the processor returns from halt. In case of applied multi core and existence of \"slave\" EcuM(s) this check should be executed on the \"master\" EcuM only. The \"master\" EcuM generates the hash out of all data that lie within its reach. Private data of \"slave\" EcuMs are out of scope."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02867",
   "text": "If Development Error Reporting is turned on and parame- ter \"sources\" contains an unknown (unconfigured) wakeup source, EcuM_SetWake- upEvent shall not update its internal variable and shall send the ECUM_E_UN- KNOWN_WAKEUP_SOURCE error message to the DET module instead."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02868",
   "text": "If Development Error Reporting is turned on and the sources parameter contains an unknown (unconfigured) wakeup source, EcuM_Validate- WakeupEvent shall ignore the call and send the ECUM_E_UNKNOWN_WAKEUP_ SOURCE error message to the DET module."
  },

  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02907",
   "text": "Service Name EcuM_AL_DriverInitOne Syntax void EcuM_AL_DriverInitOne ( void ) Service ID [hex] 0x33 Sync/Async Synchronous Reentrancy Non Reentrant Parameters (in) None Parameters (inout) None Parameters (out) None Return value None Description This callout shall provide driver initialization and other hardware-related startup activities in case of a power on reset.   },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02928",

  },
  {

It shall also be called by the ISR of a wakeup source to set up the PLL and check other wakeup sources that may be connected to the same interrupt. Avai…"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02932",
   "text": "When activated through the EcuM_StartupTwo (see [SWS_EcuM_02838] ) function, the ECU Manager module shall perform the actions in StartPostOS Sequence (see table 7.2)."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02947",
   "text": "For re-initialization during WakeupRestart, the integrator shall integrate a restart block into the integration code for EcuM_AL_DriverRestart (see [SWS_EcuM_02923] ) using the EcuMDriverRestartList ."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02951",
   "text": "In contrast to the SHUTDOWN phase, the ECU Manager mod- ule shall not shut down the OS when entering the SLEEP phase. The sleep mode, i.e. combination of the EcuM SLEEP phase and the Mcu Mode, shall be transparent to the OS."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02952",
   "text": "As its last activity, the ECU Manager module shall call the Shut- downOS function."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02953",
   "text": "The shutdown hook shall call EcuM_Shutdown (see [SWS_EcuM_02812] ) to terminate the shutdown process. EcuM_Shutdown (see [SWS_EcuM_02812] ) shall not return but switch off the ECU or issue a reset."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02957",
   "text": "The ECU Manager module may define a configurable set of sleep modes (see EcuMSleepMode ) where each mode itself is a shutdown target."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02958",
   "text": "The ECU Manager module shall allow mapping the MCU sleep modes to ECU sleep modes and hence allow them to be addressed as shutdown tar- gets."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02960",
   "text": "The ECU Manager module shall execute the Halt Sequence in sleep modes that halt the microcontroller. In these sleep modes the ECU Manager module does not execute any code."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02961",
   "text": "The ECU Manager module shall invoke the EcuM_Generat- eRamHash (see [SWS_EcuM_02919] ) where the system designer can place a RAM integrity check."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02962",
   "text": "The ECU Manager module shall execute the Poll Sequence in sleep modes that reduce the power consumption of the microcontroller but still execute code."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02963",
   "text": "If a wakeup event (e.g. toggling a wakeup line, communication on a CAN bus etc.) occurs while the ECU is in Halt or Poll, then the ECU Manager module shall regain control and exit the SLEEP phase by executing the WakeupRestart sequence. An ISR may be invoked to handle the wakeup event, but this depends on the hardware and the driver implementation."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02975",
   "text": "If a wakeup event requires validation then the ECU Manager module shall invoke the validation protocol"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02976",
   "text": "If a wakeup event does not require validation, the ECU Man- ager module shall issue a mode switch request to set the event's mode to ECUM_ WKSTATUS_VALIDATED."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02979",
   "text": "The shutdownMode parameter shall determine the specific sleep or reset mode (see ECUC_EcuM_00132) relevant to SelectShutdownTarget, GetShutdownTarget and GetLastShutdownTarget. The ECU Manager module shall only use the shutdownMode parameter is if the shutdownTarget parameter is equal to ECUM_SHUTDOWN_TARGET_SLEEP or ECUM_SHUTDOWN_TARGET_RESET, otherwise it shall be ignored."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02980",
   "text": "The ECU Manager module shall ignore all types of errors that occur during initialization, e.g. values returned by init functions"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02987",
   "text": "When the RAM check fails on wakeup the ECU Manager mod- ule shall invoke EcuM_ErrorHook with the parameter ECUM_E_RAM_CHECK_FAILED . It is left integrator's discretion to allow EcuM_ErrorHook to relay the error to the DEM when he judges that the DEM will not write damaged NVRAM blocks."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_02990",
   "text": "The ECU Manager module implementation shall provide a sin- gle EcuM_Callout_Stubs.c file which contains the stubs of the callouts realized in this implementation."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_03000",
   "text": "Caveat for the function EcuM_SelectBootTarget : This ser- vice may depend on the boot loader used. This service is only intended for use by SW-C's related to diagnostics (boot management)."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_03003",
   "text": "Caveat of EcuM_GetPendingWakeupEvents : This function only returns the wakeup events with status ECUM_WKSTATUS_PENDING."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_03009",
   "text": "If Development Error Detection is enabled for this module, then all functions shall test input parameters and running conditions and use the following error codes in an adequate way: • ECUM_E_UNINIT • ECUM_E_SERVICE_DISABLED • ECUM_E_PARAM_POINTER • ECUM_E_INVALID_PAR Specific development errors are listed in the functions, where they apply."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_03010",
   "text": "When operating on a multicore ECU ECUM shall reserve a ded- icated resource (RES_AUTOSAR_ECUM) for each core, which is allocated during Go Sleep."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_03011",
   "text": "Name EcuM_ShutdownTarget Comment A SW-C can select a shutdown target using this interface IsService true Variation  0 E_OK Operation successful Possible Errors 1 E_NOT_OK Operation failed 142 of 210 Document ID 78: AUTOSAR_SWS_ECUStateManager Specification of ECU State Manager AUTOSAR CP R20-11 Operation GetLastShutdownTarget Comment Returns the shutdown target of the previous shutdown Variation  shutdownTarget Type EcuM_ShutdownTargetType Direction OUT Comment The shutdown target of the previous shutdown Variation  shutdownMode Type EcuM_ShutdownModeType Direction OUT Comment The sleep mo…"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_03012",
   "text": "Name EcuM_BootTarget Comment A SW-C that wants to select a boot target must use the client-server interface EcuM_Boot Target. IsService true Variation  0 E_OK Operation successful Possible Errors 1 E_NOT_OK Operation failed Operation GetBootTarget Comment Returns the current boot target Variation  target Type EcuM_BootTargetType Direction OUT Comment The currently selected boot target Parameters Variation  Possible Errors E_OK Operation SelectBootTarget Comment Selects a boot target Variation  target Type EcuM_BootTargetType Direction IN Comment The selected boot target Parameters Variati…"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_03017",
   "text": "Name AlarmClock_{UserName} Kind ProvidedPort Interface EcuM_AlarmClock Description Provides to SW-Cs an alarm clock. The EcuM_AlarmClock port uses port-defined argument values to identify the user that manages its alarm clock. Type EcuM_UserType Port Defined Argument Value(s) Value {ecuc(EcuM/EcuMConfiguration/EcuMFlexConfiguration/EcuMFlexUser Config/EcuMFlexUser.value)} Variation {ecuc(EcuM/EcuMFlexGeneral/EcuMAlarmClockPresent)} == true UserName = {ecuc(EcuM/EcuMConfiguration/EcuMFlexConfiguration/EcuMAlarm Clock.SHORT-NAME)}"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_03018",
   "text": "The definition of the internal behavior of the the ECU Manager module shall be as follows. This detailed description is only needed for the configura- tion of the local RTE. InternalBehavior EcuStateManager { // Runnable entities of the EcuStateManager RunnableEntity SelectShutdownTarget symbol \"EcuM_SelectShutdownTarget\" canbeInvokedConcurrently = TRUE RunnableEntity GetShutdownTarget 91 of 210 Document ID 78: AUTOSAR_SWS_ECUStateManager Specification of ECU State Manager AUTOSAR CP R20-11 symbol \"EcuM_GetShutdownTarget\" canbeInvokedConcurrently = TRUE RunnableEntity GetLastShutdownTarget sy…"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_03019",
   "text": "ECUM_E_EARLIER_ACTIVE and ECUM_E_PAST shall be of type Std_ReturnType and represent the following values • ECUM_E_EARLIER_ACTIVE = 3 • ECUM_E_PAST = 4"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_03020",
   "text": "In the Poll sequence the EcuM shall call the callouts EcuM_- SleepActivity and EcuM_CheckWakeup () in a blocking loop until a pending/vali- dated wakeup event is reported."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_03021",
   "text": "See 7.4"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_03022",
   "text": "The SHUTDOWN phase handles the controlled shutdown of basic software modules and finally results in the selected shutdown target OFF or RESET."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_03023",
   "text": "If development error detection is enabled and EcuM_Re- leaseRUN did not find a previous matching request for the provided user, then the function shall report ECUM_E_MISMATCHED_RUN_RELEASE to Det."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_03024",
   "text": "If development error detection is enabled and there are multiple requests by the same user detected by EcuM_RequestRUN the function shall report ECUM_E_MULTIPLE_RUN_REQUESTS to Det."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_03025",
   "text": "If development error detection is enabled and there are multiple requests by the same user detected by EcuM_RequestPOST_RUN the function shall report ECUM_E_MULTIPLE_RUN_REQUESTS to Det."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_03026",
   "text": "If development error detection is enabled and EcuM_Release- POST_RUN did not find a previous matching request for the provided user, then the function shall report ECUM_E_MISMATCHED_RUN_RELEASE to Det."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04001",
   "text": "If irregular events (a hardware reset or a power cycle) occur while the ECU is in Halt or Poll, the ECU Manager module shall restart the ECU in the STARTUP phase."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04002",
   "text": "When the Alarm Clock service is present (see EcuMAlarm- ClockPresent ) the EcuM_MainFunction shall update the Alarm Clock Timer"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04003",
   "text": "When an ECU Manager action causes the state of a wakeup source to change, the ECU Manager module shall issue a mode request to the BswM to change the wakeup source's mode to the new the wakeup source state."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04004",
   "text": "The ECU Manager Module shall either provide a single wakeup validation timeout timer or one timer per wakeup source."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04005",
   "text": "The ECU Manager module shall define a configurable set of reset modes (see EcuMResetMode and EcuM_ResetType ), where each mode itself is a shutdown target. The set will minimally contain targets for • Mcu_PerformReset • WdgM_PerformReset • Toggle I/O Pin via DIO / SPI"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04006",
   "text": "The ECU Manager module shall allow defining aliases for reset targets (See EcuM180_Conf)."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04007",
   "text": "The ECU Manager module shall define a configurable set of reset causes (see EcuMShutdownCause and EcuM_ShutdownCauseType ). The set shall minimally contain targets for • ECU state machine entered a shutdown state • WdgM detected a failure • DCM requests shutdownI and the time of the reset."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04008",
   "text": "The ECU Manager Module shall offer facilities to BSW modules and SW-Cs to • Record a shutdown cause • Get a set of recent shutdown causes"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04009",
   "text": "When leaving the Sleep state the ECU Manager Module will abort any active user alarm clock and the master alarm clock. This means that both clock induced and wakeups due to other events will result in clearing all alarms."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04010",
   "text": "User alarms and the master alarm shall be cancelled during the StartPreOS Sequence, in the WakeupRestart Sequence and the OffPreOS Se- quence."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04011",
   "text": "The EcuM_MainFunction shall run in all EcuM instances."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04012",
   "text": "Each instance of the ECU Manager module shall process the wakeup events of its core."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04014",
   "text": "The ECU Manager module shall call BswM_Init for all core local BswMs on the master and all slave cores."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04015",
   "text": "74 of 210 Document ID 78: AUTOSAR_SWS_ECUStateManager Specification of ECU State Manager AUTOSAR CP R20-11 Figure 7.19: Master Core StartPreOS Sequence"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04016",
   "text": "75 of 210 Document ID 78: AUTOSAR_SWS_ECUStateManager Specification of ECU State Manager AUTOSAR CP R20-11 Figure 7.20: Master Core StartPostOS Sequence"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04017",
   "text": "76 of 210 Document ID 78: AUTOSAR_SWS_ECUStateManager Specification of ECU State Manager AUTOSAR CP R20-11 Figure 7.21: Slave Core StartPreOS Sequence"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04018",
   "text": "77 of 210 Document ID 78: AUTOSAR_SWS_ECUStateManager Specification of ECU State Manager AUTOSAR CP R20-11 Figure 7.22: Slave Core StartPostOS Sequence"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04020",
   "text": "Figure 7.24: Master Core OffPostOS Sequence"
  },
  {

  },
  {

  },

  },
  {

   "text": "Figure 7.29: Master Core Poll Sequence"
  },
  {

  },

  },

  {

   "text": "Type of error Related error code Error value Multiple requests by the same user were detected ECUM_E_MULTIPLE_RUN_REQUESTS Assigned by Implementation A function was called which was disabled by configuration ECUM_E_SERVICE_DISABLED Assigned by Implementation A service was called prior to initialization ECUM_E_UNINIT Assigned by Implementation 5 97 of 210 Document ID 78: AUTOSAR_SWS_ECUStateManager Specification of ECU State Manager AUTOSAR CP R20-11 4 Type of error Related error code Error value An unknown wakeup source was passed as a parameter to an API ECUM_E_UNKNOWN_WAKEUP_SOURCE Assigned…"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04033",
   "text": "In the unrecoverable error situations defined in the first column of Table in [SWS_EcuM_04032], the ECU Manager module shall call the EcuM_Er- rorHook callout with the parameter value set to the corresponding related error code."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04038",
   "text": "Name EcuM_ConfigType Kind Structure - Type  Elements Comment The content of this structure depends on the post-build configuration of EcuM. Description A pointer to such a structure shall be provided to the ECU State Manager initialization routine for configuration. Available via EcuM.h"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04040",
   "text": "Name EcuM_WakeupSourceType Kind Type Derived from uint32 ECUM_WKSOURCE_POWER 0x01 Power cycle (bit 0) ECUM_WKSOURCE_RESET (default) 0x02 Hardware reset (bit 1). If the Mcu driver cannot distinguish between a power cycle and a reset reason, then this shall be the default wakeup source. 5 101 of 210 Document ID 78: AUTOSAR_SWS_ECUStateManager Specification of ECU State Manager AUTOSAR CP R20-11 4 ECUM_WKSOURCE_ INTERNAL_RESET 0x04 Internal reset of \u0016 C (bit 2) The internal reset typically only resets the \u0016 C core but not peripherals or memory controllers. The exact behavior is hardware specific…"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04041",
   "text": "Name EcuM_WakeupStatusType Kind Type Derived from uint8 ECUM_WKSTATUS_NONE 0 No pending wakeup event was detected ECUM_WKSTATUS_PENDING 1 The wakeup event was detected but not yet validated ECUM_WKSTATUS_VALIDATED 2 The wakeup event is valid Range ECUM_WKSTATUS_EXPIRED 3 The wakeup event has not been validated and has expired therefore Description The type describes the possible states of a wakeup source. Available via EcuM.h"
  },

EcuM_SetRelW…"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04055",
   "text": "If the relative time from now is earlier than the current wakeup time, EcuM_SetRelWakeupAlarm shall update the wakeup time."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04056",
   "text": "If the relative time from now is later than the current wakeup time, EcuM_SetRelWakeupAlarm shall not update the wakeup time and shall return ECUM_E_EARLIER_ACTIVE."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04057",

Parameters (in) time Absolute time in seconds. Note that, absolute alarms use knowledge of the current time. Parameters (inout) None Parameters (out) None Return value Std_ReturnType E_OK: The service has succeeded E_NOT_OK: The service failed ECUM_E_EARLIER_ACTIVE: An earlier alarm is already set ECUM_E_PAST: The given point in time has already passed Desc…"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04058",
   "text": "If the time parameter is earlier than the current wakeup time, EcuM_SetAbsWakeupAlarm shall update the wakeup time."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04059",
   "text": "If the time parameter is later than the current wakeup time, EcuM_SetAbsWakeupAlarm shall not update the wakeup time and shall return ECUM_E_EARLIER_ACTIVE."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04060",
   "text": "If the time parameter is earlier than now, EcuM_SetAbsWake- upAlarm shall not update the wakeup time and shall return ECUM_E_PAST."
  },
  {

  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04065",
   "text": "Service Name EcuM_AL_Reset Syntax void EcuM_AL_Reset ( EcuM_ResetType reset ) Service ID [hex] 0x4C Sync/Async Synchronous Reentrancy Non Reentrant Parameters (in) reset Type of reset to be performed. Parameters (inout) None Parameters (out) None Return value None 5 130 of 210 Document ID 78: AUTOSAR_SWS_ECUStateManager Specification of ECU State Manager AUTOSAR CP R20-11 4 Description This callout shall take the code for resetting the ECU. Available via EcuM_Externals.h"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04066",
   "text": "Figure 7.14: WakeupRestart Sequence"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04069",
   "text": "When the Alarm Clock service is present (see EcuMAlarm- ClockPresent ) the EcuM Manager module shall maintain an EcuM clock whose time shall be the time in seconds since battery connect."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04070",
   "text": "Each EcuM User shall have at most one user alarm clock."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04071",
   "text": "An EcuM User shall not be able to set the value of another user's alarm clock."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04072",
   "text": "The ECU Manager module shall set always the master alarm clock value to the value of the earliest user alarm clock value."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04073",
   "text": "Only authorized EcuM Users can set the EcuM clock time (see EcuMSetClockAllowedUsers )."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04074",
   "text": "When the shutdown target is RESET, the ECU Manager module shall call the EcuM_AL_Reset callout."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04075",
   "text": "When the shutdown target is OFF, the ECU Manager module shall call the EcuM_AL_SwitchOff callout."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04076",
   "text": "EcuM_GetExpiredWakeupEvents shall return wakeup events which have been set to validated in the internal expired events variable as bits set in a EcuM_WakeupSourceType bitmask."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04078",
   "text": "EcuM_ValidateWakeupEvent sets (OR-operation) all events passed as a bit set in the sources in parameter (EcuM_WakeupSourceType bitmask) in the internal validated wakeup events variable."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04079",
   "text": "EcuMValidateWakeupEvent shall invoke BswM_EcuM_Current Wakeup with its sources parameter and state value ECUM_WKSTATUS_VALIDATED."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04080",
   "text": "The ECU Manager module shall derive the wakeup sources to be checked (and used as the wakeupSource parameter) from the EcuMWakeup Source (see ECUC_EcuM_00152) bitfield configured for the current sleep mode. The integration code used for this callout must determine which wakeup sources must be checked."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04081",
   "text": "When the validation timeout expires for a pending wakeup event, the EcuM_MainFunction sets (OR-operation) set the bit in the internal expired wakeup events variable."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04082",
   "text": "When the validation timeout expires for a pending wakeup event, the EcuM_MainFunction shall invoke BswM_EcuM_Current_Wakeup with an EcuM_WakeupSourceType bitmask parameter with the bit corresponding to the wakeup event set and state value parameter set to ECUM_WKSTATUS_EXPIRED."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04084",
   "text": "The ECU Manager module shall derive the wakeup sources to be disabled (and used as the wakeupSource parameter) from the internal pend- ing events variable (NOT operation). The integration code used for this callout must determine which wakeup sources must be disabled."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04085",
   "text": "Service Name EcuM_AL_SetProgrammableInterrupts Syntax void EcuM_AL_SetProgrammableInterrupts ( void ) Service ID [hex] 0x4A Sync/Async Asynchronous Reentrancy Non Reentrant Parameters (in) None Parameters (inout) None Parameters (out) None Return value None 5 125 of 210 Document ID 78: AUTOSAR_SWS_ECUStateManager Specification of ECU State Manager AUTOSAR CP R20-11 4 Description If the configuration parameter EcuMSetProgrammableInterrupts is set to true, this callout Ecu M_AL_SetProgrammableInterrupts is executed and shall set the interrupts on ECUs with programmable interrupts. Available via…"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04086",
   "text": "The EcuM clock shall track time in the UP and SLEEP phases."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04087",
   "text": "Hardware permitting, the EcuM clock time shall not be reset by an ECU reset."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04088",
   "text": "There shall be one and only one wakeup source assigned to the EcuM Clock (see EcuMAlarmWakeupSource )."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04089",
   "text": "If the underlying hardware mechanism is tick based, the ECUM shall \"correct\" the time accordingly"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04091",
   "text": "The wakeup sources can be in the following states: State Description NONE No wakeup event was detected or has been cleared. PENDING A wakeup event was detected but not yet validated. VALIDATED A wakeup event was detected and succesfully validated. EXPIRED A wakeup event was detected but validation failed. Table 7.7: Wakeup sources"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04092",
   "text": "The ShutdownTarget Sleep shall put the all cores into sleep."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04093",
   "text": "The ECU Manager module shall start the SchM and the OS on every core."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04094",
   "text": "In the case of a MultiCore ECU, the EcuM AUTOSAR service (Standardized AUTOSAR Interfaces) may be offered on one or more cores."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04095",
   "text": "In the case of a MultiCore ECU, the EcuM C-API Interfaces (Standardized Interfaces) which are used by other BSW modules shall be offered in every partition a EcuM runs in."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04096",
   "text": "Service Name EcuM_StartCheckWakeup Syntax void EcuM_StartCheckWakeup ( EcuM_WakeupSourceType WakeupSource ) Service ID [hex] 0x00 Sync/Async Synchronous Reentrancy Non Reentrant Parameters (in) WakeupSource For this wakeup source the corresponding CheckWakeupTimer shall be started. Parameters (inout) None Parameters (out) None Return value None Description This API is called by the ECU Firmware to start the CheckWakeupTimer for the corresponding WakeupSource. If EcuMCheckWakeupTimeout > 0 the CheckWakeupTimer for the Wakeup Source is started. If EcuMCheckWakeupTimeout <= 0 the API call is ign…"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04098",
   "text": "If EcuM_SetWakeupEvent is called for the corresponding wakeup source the CheckWakeupTimer is cancelled."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04101",
   "text": "154 of 210 Document ID 78: AUTOSAR_SWS_ECUStateManager Specification of ECU State Manager AUTOSAR CP R20-11 Name EcuM_ShutdownModeType Kind Type Derived from uint16 {ecuc(EcuM/EcuMConfiguration/ EcuMFlexConfiguration/Ecu MResetMode.SHORT-NAME)} {256 + ecuc(EcuM/Ecu MConfiguration/Ecu MFlexConfiguration/ EcuMResetMode.Ecu MResetModeId)} Configured Reset Modes Range {ecuc(EcuM/EcuMConfiguration/ EcuMCommonConfiguration/Ecu MSleepMode.SHORT-NAME)} {ecuc(EcuM/ Ecu MConfiguration/Ecu MCommon Configuration/Ecu MSleepMode.Ecu MSleepModeId)} Configured Sleep Modes Description This data type represent…"

  },
  {

  },

Variation UserName = {ecuc(EcuM/EcuMConfiguration/EcuMFlexConfiguration/EcuMFlexUserConfig/Ecu MFlexUser.SHORT-NAME)}"
  },

Variation UserName = {ecuc(EcuM/EcuMConfiguration/EcuMFlexConfiguration/EcuMFlexUserConfig/Ecu MFlexUser.SHORT-NAME)}"
  },

  },

   "text": "152 of 210 Document ID 78: AUTOSAR_SWS_ECUStateManager Specification of ECU State Manager AUTOSAR CP R20-11 Name time Kind ProvidedPort Interface EcuM_Time Description Provides the EcuM's time service to SWCs Variation "
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04114",
   "text": "EcuM_AL_DriverInitBswM_<x> is generated for every config- ured EcuMDriverInitListBswM. The name of the generated functions shall be EcuM_ AL_DriverInitBswM_<x>, where <x> represents the short name of the EcuMDriverInit ListBswM container."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04115",
   "text": "ECU Mode Handling shall be applied when EcuMModeHan- dling is configured to true."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04116",
   "text": "When the BswM sets a state of the EcuM by EcuM_SetState , the EcuM shall indicate the corresponding mode to the RTE."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04117",
   "text": "When the last RUN request has been released, ECU State Manager module shall indicate this to BswM using the API BswM_EcuM_- RequestedState(ECUM_STATE_APP_RUN, ECUM_RUNSTATUS_RELEASED) ."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04118",
   "text": "When the ECU State Manager is not in the state which is re- quested by a SWC, it shall inform BswM about requested states using the BswM_- EcuM_RequestedState API."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04119",
   "text": "When the last POST_RUN request has been released, ECU State Manager module shall indicate this to BswM using the API BswM_EcuM_Re- questedState(ECUM_STATE_APP_POST_RUN, ECUM_RUNSTATUS_RELEASED) ."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04120",
   "text": "Name EcuM_RunStatusType Kind Type Derived from uint8 ECUM_RUNSTATUS_UNKNOWN 0 Unknown status. Init Value. ECUM_RUNSTATUS_ REQUESTED 1 Status requested from EcuM Range ECUM_RUNSTATUS_ RELEASED 2 Status released from EcuM. Description Result of the Run Request Protocol sent to BswM Available via EcuM.h"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04121",
   "text": "The ECU Manager module shall inform BswM about the state of the Run Request Protocol as listed in the EcuM_RunStatusType."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04122",
   "text": "Service Name EcuM_SetState Syntax void EcuM_SetState ( EcuM_StateType state ) Service ID [hex] 0x2b Sync/Async Synchronous Reentrancy Reentrant Parameters (in) state State indicated by BswM. Parameters (inout) None Parameters (out) None Return value None Description Function called by BswM to notify about State Switch. Available via EcuM.h"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04123",
   "text": "The EcuM_SetState function shall set the EcuM State to the value of the State parameter. If the State parameter is not a valid value, the EcuM_SetState function shall not change the State and if Development Error Reporting is turned on, the EcuM_SetState function shall additionally send an ECUM_E_STATE_PAR_OUT_OF_RANGE error message to the DET module."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04124",
   "text": "Service Name EcuM_RequestRUN Syntax Std_ReturnType EcuM_RequestRUN ( EcuM_UserType user ) Service ID [hex] 0x03 Sync/Async Synchronous Reentrancy Reentrant Parameters (in) user ID of the entity requesting the RUN state. Parameters (inout) None Parameters (out) None 5 107 of 210 Document ID 78: AUTOSAR_SWS_ECUStateManager Specification of ECU State Manager AUTOSAR CP R20-11 4 Return value Std_ReturnType E_OK: The request was accepted by EcuM. E_NOT_OK: The request was not accepted by EcuM Description Places a request for the RUN state. Requests can be placed by every user made known to the sta…"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04125",
   "text": "Requests of EcuM_RequestRUN cannot be nested, i.e. one user can only place one request but not more. Additional or duplicate user requests by the same user shall be reported to DET. Of course the DET will only be notified under development conditions."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04126",
   "text": "An implementation must track requests for each user known on the ECU. Run requests are specific to the user."
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04127",
   "text": "Service Name EcuM_ReleaseRUN Syntax Std_ReturnType EcuM_ReleaseRUN ( EcuM_UserType user ) Service ID [hex] 0x04 Sync/Async Synchronous Reentrancy Reentrant Parameters (in) user ID of the entity releasing the RUN state. The service is intended for implementing AUTOSAR ports. Available via EcuM.h"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04128",
   "text": "Service Name EcuM_RequestPOST_RUN Syntax Std_ReturnType EcuM_RequestPOST_RUN ( EcuM_UserType user ) Service ID [hex] 0x0a Sync/Async Synchronous Reentrancy Reentrant Parameters (in) user ID of the entity requesting the POST RUN state. Parameters (inout) None Parameters (out) None Return value Std_ReturnType E_OK: The request was accepted by EcuM E_NOT_OK: The request was not accepted by EcuM Description Places a request for the POST RUN state. Requests can be placed by every user made known to the state manager at configuration time. Requests for RUN and POST RUN must be tracked independently…"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04129",
   "text": "Service Name EcuM_ReleasePOST_RUN Syntax Std_ReturnType EcuM_ReleasePOST_RUN ( EcuM_UserType user ) Service ID [hex] 0x0b Sync/Async Synchronous Reentrancy Reentrant 5 109 of 210 Document ID 78: AUTOSAR_SWS_ECUStateManager Specification of ECU State Manager AUTOSAR CP R20-11 4 Parameters (in) user ID of the entity releasing the POST RUN state. Parameters (inout) None Parameters (out) None Return value Std_ReturnType E_OK: The release request was accepted by EcuM E_NOT_OK: The release request was not accepted by EcuM Description Releases a POST RUN request previously done with a call to EcuM_R…"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04130",
   "text": "The ECU State Manager module shall provide System Services for the following functionalities when the container EcuMModeHandling (see 10.2.1) is available: • requesting RUN • releasing RUN • requesting POST_RUN • releasing POST_RUN"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04131",
   "text": "Name EcuM_StateRequest Comment Interface to request a specific ECU state IsService true Variation  0 E_OK Operation successful Possible Errors 1 E_NOT_OK Operation failed Operation ReleasePOSTRUN Comment  Variation  Possible Errors E_OK E_NOT_OK Operation ReleaseRUN Comment  Variation  Possible Errors E_OK E_NOT_OK Operation RequestPOSTRUN Comment  Variation  Possible Errors E_OK E_NOT_OK 149 of 210 Document ID 78: AUTOSAR_SWS_ECUStateManager Specification of ECU State Manager AUTOSAR CP R20-11 Operation RequestRUN Comment  Variation  Possible Errors E_OK E_NOT_OK"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04132",
   "text": "The mode port of the ECU State Manager module shall declare the following modes: • STARTUP • RUN • POST_RUN • SLEEP • SHUTDOWN"
  },
  {
   "id": "SWS_EcuM_04133",
   "text": "Mode changes shall be notified to SW-Cs through the RTE mode ports when the mode change occurs. This specification assumes that the port name is currentMode and that the direct API of RTE will be used. Under these conditions mode changes signaled by invoking Rte_StatusType Rte_Switch_currentMode_currentMode( Rte_ModeType_EcuM_Mode mode) where mode is the new mode to be notified. The value range is specified by the previ- ous requirement. The return value shall be ignored. A SW-C which wants to be notified of mode changes should require the mode switch interface EcuM_CurrentMode."
  },

<h4>Rolle und Systemgrenzen des ECU State Managers im AUTOSAR-Gesamtsystem</h4>
<p>Der ECU State Manager (<code>EcuM</code>) übernimmt im klassischen AUTOSAR-Schichtenmodell die zentrale Verantwortung für den Lebenszyklus des Steuergeräts von der ersten Hardware-Initialisierung nach einem Reset bis hin zum kontrollierten Abschalten oder Übergang in stromsparende Schlafmodi <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02811" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02811">[SWS_EcuM_02811]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_03022" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_03022">[SWS_EcuM_03022]</a>. Während in früheren AUTOSAR-Releases das gesamte Betriebsmanagement monolithisch im EcuM gebündelt war, delegiert das flexible Architekturmodell die fein granulare Zustandslogik während der Betriebsphase weitgehend an den BSW Mode Manager (<code>BswM</code>) <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04115" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04115">[SWS_EcuM_04115]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04116" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04116">[SWS_EcuM_04116]</a>. Der EcuM konzentriert sich auf die Phasen ohne voll verfügbares Betriebssystem sowie auf die hardwarenahen Umschaltsequenzen.</p>

<p>Zu den Nachbarmodulen des EcuM gehören auf unterer Ebene der Microcontroller Abstraction Layer (MCAL, insbesondere Treiber wie MCU, PORT, DIO, Fls, Can, Eth, Fr, Lin und GPT) <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02810" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02810">[SWS_EcuM_02810]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02859" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02859">[SWS_EcuM_02859]</a>, auf Systemebene das Betriebssystem (OS) <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02603" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02603">[SWS_EcuM_02603]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02952" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02952">[SWS_EcuM_02952]</a>, der BswM <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02858" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02858">[SWS_EcuM_02858]</a>, der ComM für netzwerkbezogene Weckanzeigen <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02645" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02645">[SWS_EcuM_02645]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04140" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04140">[SWS_EcuM_04140]</a> sowie der Default Error Tracer (DET) <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_03009" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_03009">[SWS_EcuM_03009]</a>. Software-Components (SW-Cs) interagieren über standardisierte AUTOSAR-Service-Ports mit dem EcuM, etwa zur Abfrage und Auswahl des Shutdown-Targets <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_03011" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_03011">[SWS_EcuM_03011]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04111" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04111">[SWS_EcuM_04111]</a>, zur Boot-Target-Selektion <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_03012" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_03012">[SWS_EcuM_03012]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04110" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04110">[SWS_EcuM_04110]</a>, für Statusanforderungen über <code>EcuM_StateRequest</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04131" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04131">[SWS_EcuM_04131]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04135" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04135">[SWS_EcuM_04135]</a> sowie zur Nutzung von Weckalarmen über Alarm-Clock-Ports <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_03017" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_03017">[SWS_EcuM_03017]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04105" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04105">[SWS_EcuM_04105]</a>.</p>

<p class="diagram-note">Kontextdiagramm: Einbettung des EcuM in das Gesamtsystem zwischen Hardware-Treibern, BSW-Diensten, OS und Applikation. Quellen: <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02810" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02810">[SWS_EcuM_02810]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02858" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02858">[SWS_EcuM_02858]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_03011" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_03011">[SWS_EcuM_03011]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04111" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04111">[SWS_EcuM_04111]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04131" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04131">[SWS_EcuM_04131]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04135" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04135">[SWS_EcuM_04135]</a></p>

<h4>Initialisierungsphasen von StartPreOS bis zur BSW-Aktivierung</h4>
<p>Die Hochlaufphase des Steuergeräts gliedert sich zwingend in zwei Abschnitte: die Phase vor dem Start des Betriebssystems (StartPreOS) und die Phase nach dem Start des Betriebssystems (StartPostOS) <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02411" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02411">[SWS_EcuM_02411]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02603" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02603">[SWS_EcuM_02603]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02932" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02932">[SWS_EcuM_02932]</a>. Der Eintritt erfolgt über den Aufruf von <code>EcuM_Init()</code>, der definitionsgemäß niemals an den Aufrufer zurückkehrt, da er am Ende der StartPreOS-Kette <code>StartOS()</code> ausführt <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02811" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02811">[SWS_EcuM_02811]</a>. In <code>EcuM_Init()</code> werden zunächst grundlegende Hardware-Callouts ausgeführt, darunter die Treiberinitialisierung von Block 0 über <code>EcuM_AL_DriverInitZero()</code> für rein vorkompilierte Module <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02559" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02559">[SWS_EcuM_02559]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02905" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02905">[SWS_EcuM_02905]</a>. Sofern konfiguriert, wird die Schleifenerkennung via <code>EcuM_LoopDetection()</code> ausgeführt <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04137" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04137">[SWS_EcuM_04137]</a>.</p>

<p>Um die gültige Post-Build-Konfiguration zu bestimmen, ruft der EcuM das Callout <code>EcuM_DeterminePbConfiguration()</code> auf <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02906" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02906">[SWS_EcuM_02906]</a>. Die gelieferte Konfigurationsstruktur <code>EcuM_ConfigType</code> enthält Versions- und Varianten-IDs sowie einen Prüf-Hashwert, der gegen <code>ECUM_CONFIGCONSISTENCY_HASH</code> validiert werden muss, bevor weitere Module gestartet werden <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02794" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02794">[SWS_EcuM_02794]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02795" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02795">[SWS_EcuM_02795]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02798" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02798">[SWS_EcuM_02798]</a>. Erst nach erfolgreicher Konsistenzprüfung über alle BSW-Post-Build-Daten hinweg <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02796" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02796">[SWS_EcuM_02796]</a> startet der EcuM die Treiber der Initialisierungsliste 1 mittels <code>EcuM_AL_DriverInitOne()</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02559" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02559">[SWS_EcuM_02559]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02907" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02907">[SWS_EcuM_02907]</a>. Hierbei werden programmierbare Interrupts konfiguriert <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04085" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04085">[SWS_EcuM_04085]</a>, der Reset-Grund ermittelt und als Weckquelle registriert <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02601" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02601">[SWS_EcuM_02601]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02623" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02623">[SWS_EcuM_02623]</a>, bestehende Weckalarme gelöscht <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04010" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04010">[SWS_EcuM_04010]</a> und alle Basissoftwaremodule initialisiert, die für das Hochfahren des OS zwingend benötigt werden <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02603" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02603">[SWS_EcuM_02603]</a>.</p>

<p>Nachdem <code>StartOS()</code> die Ausführung an das Betriebssystem übergeben hat, startet das System einen konfigurierten Autostart-Task oder expliziten Initialisierungs-Task, dessen erste Pflicht die Ausführung von <code>EcuM_StartupTwo()</code> ist <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02806" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02806">[SWS_EcuM_02806]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02838" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02838">[SWS_EcuM_02838]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_02932" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_02932">[SWS_EcuM_02932]</a>. In dieser StartPostOS-Sequenz startet der EcuM den Schedule Manager (SchM) sowie den BswM via <code>BswM_Init()</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04014" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04014">[SWS_EcuM_04014]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04093" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04093">[SWS_EcuM_04093]</a>. Die weitere Initialisierung nachgelagerter BSW-Module wird anschließend über BSW-Init-Listen durch <code>EcuM_AL_DriverInitBswM_&lt;x&gt;()</code> ausgeführt, gesteuert durch den BswM <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04114" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04114">[SWS_EcuM_04114]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04142" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04142">[SWS_EcuM_04142]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_91001" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_91001">[SWS_EcuM_91001]</a>.</p>

<h4>Modusverwaltung und das Run-Request-Protokoll im Zusammenspiel mit dem BswM</h4>
<p>Wenn die Modusverwaltung (<code>EcuMModeHandling</code>) aktiv ist, verwaltet der EcuM die standardisierten Systemmodi STARTUP, RUN, POST_RUN, SLEEP und SHUTDOWN <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04107" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04107">[SWS_EcuM_04107]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04115" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04115">[SWS_EcuM_04115]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04132" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04132">[SWS_EcuM_04132]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_91005" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_91005">[SWS_EcuM_91005]</a>. Software-Komponenten und BSW-Module fordern die Betriebsbereitschaft über das Run-Request-Protokoll an. Hierzu stellt der EcuM die APIs <code>EcuM_RequestRUN()</code> und <code>EcuM_ReleaseRUN()</code> sowie <code>EcuM_RequestPOST_RUN()</code> und <code>EcuM_ReleasePOST_RUN()</code> bereit <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04124" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04124">[SWS_EcuM_04124]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04127" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04127">[SWS_EcuM_04127]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04128" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04128">[SWS_EcuM_04128]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04129" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04129">[SWS_EcuM_04129]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04130" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04130">[SWS_EcuM_04130]</a>.</p>

<p>Das Protokoll überwacht jeden Benutzer (<code>EcuM_UserType</code>) individuell <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04126" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04126">[SWS_EcuM_04126]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_91004" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_91004">[SWS_EcuM_91004]</a>. Verschachtelte Anfragen desselben Benutzers sind unzulässig und führen im Entwicklungsmodus zu Fehlermeldungen an das DET <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_03024" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_03024">[SWS_EcuM_03024]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_03025" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_03025">[SWS_EcuM_03025]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04125" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04125">[SWS_EcuM_04125]</a>. Ebenso wird das Freigeben eines nicht gehaltenen Zustands gemeldet <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_03023" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_03023">[SWS_EcuM_03023]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_03026" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_03026">[SWS_EcuM_03026]</a>. Sobald die erste RUN- oder POST_RUN-Anforderung eingeht, meldet der EcuM dies an den BswM mittels <code>BswM_EcuM_RequestedState(..., ECUM_RUNSTATUS_REQUESTED)</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04118" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04118">[SWS_EcuM_04118]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04120" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04120">[SWS_EcuM_04120]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04121" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04121">[SWS_EcuM_04121]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04144" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04144">[SWS_EcuM_04144]</a>. Werden alle Anforderungen für RUN bzw. POST_RUN freigegeben, erfolgt die Abmeldung über <code>ECUM_RUNSTATUS_RELEASED</code> <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04117" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04117">[SWS_EcuM_04117]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04119" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04119">[SWS_EcuM_04119]</a>.</p>

<p>Der BswM evaluiert die Anfragen im Rahmen seiner Regelwerke und schaltet den EcuM über <code>EcuM_SetState()</code> in den entsprechenden Zustand <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04122" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04122">[SWS_EcuM_04122]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04123" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04123">[SWS_EcuM_04123]</a>. Der EcuM spiegelt Zustandswechsel über den RTE-Modusport <code>currentMode</code> an die Applikations-SW-Cs wider (<code>Rte_Switch_currentMode_currentMode</code>) <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04108" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04108">[SWS_EcuM_04108]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04112" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04112">[SWS_EcuM_04112]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04116" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04116">[SWS_EcuM_04116]</a>, <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04133" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04133">[SWS_EcuM_04133]</a> und meldet dem BswM nach Empfang der RTE-Quittung den neuen Status mittels <code>BswM_EcuM_CurrentState()</code> zurück <a class="spec-record-ref" data-req="SWS_EcuM_04143" href="../../spec/record.html?id=SWS_EcuM_04143">[SWS_EcuM_04143]</a>.</p>
